items.reviewedFinding: The clock hand marking hours/minutes on a dial is explicitly recorded separately from sewing needles and other pointed objects.
The intransitive clock/bell chiming use is distinct from transitive public announcement; the soul/body clock analogy uses audible chiming.
The impersonal construction denotes right, duty or propriety, separately from property and group relationship. Source il ne m’appartient pas denies the speaker’s place/right to act.
The pronominal verb may mean doing no more and remaining at that point; source je me contente de croire is not a feminine adjective.

Transmission of a property, power or motion is recorded separately from making information known. Source imparting thought to matter is a contextual faculty-transmission reading, without approving the theological claim.
The complete named cap of learned professions, including masters in theology, is recorded; use a full noun-phrase bank rather than treating the cap as a strict geometric assertion.
Named saints such as saint Pierre and saint Augustin occur in the adjective section; stand-alone saint nouns are separate. Source before Thomas receives proper adjective ownership.
The feminine noun includes comprehensive works synthesizing a field, with Thomas’s title explicitly recorded, separately from money and numerical addition.
The adjective includes figurative laughter that cannot be stopped alongside literal unquenchable fire; the Homeric example explains the allusion without verifying an exact quotation.

The indexed primary entry records excessive laughter to the point of breathlessness. Source is contextual humorous hyperbole, not concealment of laughter, suppression of evidence or a medical diagnosis.
